page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-focused instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, providing 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated threads. The processor cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. System memory measures 16.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per virtual core. The instance has no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage, and includes a 5 Gbps baseline network interface without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Instruction set support includes AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA extensions.

Performance across synthetic and compute-heavy benchmarks demonstrates consistent mid-tier execution. The instance scores 1585.0 in single-core Geekbench and 5889.0 in multi-core Geekbench, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11379.98. Uncached memory throughput reaches 56.88 GB/sec for sequential reads and 38.8 GB/sec for writes. The platform delivers capable throughput for software builds, scoring 8136.0 in Clang compilation tests, and achieves 43.15 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Performance drops sharply on machine learning workloads without hardware accelerators: while smaller 135M parameter models process at 765.98 tokens per second, 7B model prompt processing drops to 16.13 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio prevents over-provisioning memory for CPU-bound tasks, optimizing resource density. However, the lack of onboard storage shifts all disk I/O over the network, requiring consideration of network bandwidth utilization. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.2xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, web serving at 11.69 GB/sec static throughput, batch transcoding, and in-memory key-value caching such as Redis, which achieves 7.95 million SET operations per second.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-focused virtual machine powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of memory. Operating under KVM virtualization, it provides a 1:2 core-to-memory balance alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reflect consistent mid-range compute output, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5889.0, PassMark CPU score of 11379.98, and static web serving throughput of 11.69 GB/sec. Cache-intensive and integer workloads perform well, demonstrating 7.95 million Redis SET operations per second and steady decompression throughput. The hardware allocation suits front-end web serving, continuous integration builds, microservices, and lightweight caching layers.
